simple.meaning: אָחַד (ʼâchad) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to unify , i.e. (figuratively) collect (one's thoughts).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Ezekiel, beginning at Ezekiel 21:21. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָחַד (H258) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָחַד (ʼâchad) / H258 is traced through Ezekiel 21:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination. He shook the arrows back and forth. He consulted the teraphim.† teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. He looked in the liver.
